card_title: Was Your Faith Deeper This Year Than Last Year?
description: A new year is one of the rare pauses where we get to ask whether we grew or just got older. Five things to sit down with before you plan anything else.
excerpt: Most of us drift into a new year without really stopping to look at the one behind us. Did I grow? Or did I just get older?
body_html:
Years ago someone asked me a question that changed how I think about a new year.

"Was your faith deeper this year than it was last year?"

I didn't have a quick answer. I wanted to say yes, but when I actually thought about it, I wasn't sure. How would I even know? What does deeper faith look like? What am I supposed to be measuring?

Most of us drift into a new year without really stopping to look at the one behind us. We post a verse, pick a word, maybe write out a few goals, and jump straight into the next twelve months. But a new year is one of the rare pauses where we actually have a chance to ask the question. Did I grow? Or did I just get older?

Before you jump into this upcoming year, it's worth actually sitting down with a few things first.

Spend a few minutes with the Lord before you plan anything else.

Before the goals, before the word of the year, before the new routines, just be with Him. No agenda. Ask Him to show you what He wants you to see about where you've been. He knows your year better than you do. If you'll give Him a few minutes of quiet, He'll show you things you wouldn't have thought of on your own.

Name what He brought you through this past year.

Look back over the last twelve months. What were the hard moments and the surprises? What were the prayers you'd almost forgotten you prayed that He actually answered? Write them down. Not for a social media post, but for you. Because remembering what He's done is one of the fastest ways to trust Him more with what's coming.

Look at how you've actually grown.

Not what you learned or what you read, but how you've actually changed. Are you quicker to forgive than you were a year ago? More generous, less reactive, more patient with your kids, more honest in your marriage, more willing to say hard things kindly? Growth shows up in character, not just in knowledge.

Think about your KPIs.

If you ran your faith life the way you run a business, what would the numbers look like? How many times did you open your Bible, and how often did you pray outside of a crisis? How many hard conversations did you actually have, and how much did you give away? Did you say yes to the things God nudged you toward? You don't have to turn your faith into a spreadsheet. But knowing what you're measuring makes it a lot easier to grow.

Remember that relationships don't happen on accident.

Not with God, not with your spouse, not with your kids, not with friends. The relationships that matter most take intention. If your faith is going to be deeper at the end of this new year than it is today, something has to look different. You have to carve out time and protect it, and you have to show up when you don't feel like it.

A deeper faith isn't going to find you. You have to go after it.

So before this new year gets busy, sit with the question. Was your faith deeper this past year than the year before? And if the honest answer is no, what are you going to do differently this year so that twelve months from now the answer is yes?

What one thing is God inviting you to do differently this year to actually grow?
question: What one thing is God inviting you to do differently this year to actually grow?
